page.layout: One page of text in a single column; running head at top; no margin notes; two epitaph poems with headings; a catchword "Quo" at the foot right.

l.i: QVum nuper gladiis & forte euaseris hoste,
Hic, Francisce, iaces, nec tamen ense iace.
Sed nec in hostili potuisti occumbere campo,
Nec fortis forti casus ab hoste cadis.
Sedibus at patriis belli simulachra cientem,
Arca in qua Parcam Mauors absconderat ipse,
Sic igitur, miserande, cadis, nec cernere longum
Illa tua licuit parta trophæa manu,
At si nobiscum & sis sors aduersa iocari,
Curistis mors est feria mixta iocis?
LAngæus ille magnus hic iacet, Lector,

page.notes: Scan is a fragment of a page; the first column of the page is at the top. Some words in the verses are doubtful due to the print (e.g. "Langaei" and "Vnus" with a possible "Vnus Mineruam"); the line "Quo" is the catchword. Ornamental initials Q and L are large woodcut letters joined to their words.
